newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-NANTES' COACH HAS MIXED EMOTIONS ABOUT EUROPEAN SPOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NANTES' COACH HAS MIXED EMOTIONS ABOUT EUROPEAN SPOT.

text.p: Nantes' coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau has mixed emotions about the possibility of European competition next season.
Since a dismal opening spell of 10 matches without victory, Nantes have rallied to third place and are now on the threshold of taking the second French spot in the European Cup next season.
"We want Europe, be it the UEFA Cup or the European Cup but we're not the only candidates," Suaudeau said. "If Monaco weren't so far off, Nantes would dream of the title."
But Suaudeau is not convinced that two teams should qualify for Europe's most prestigious trophy.
"For me, it's (only) the champions who should take part in the Champions' League, not the runners-up," he said.
"I wouldn't feel we were champions if eventually we took part. This second qualifying place is a question of money. Let sports people make no mistake about that."
Nantes' steady climb up the first division table has been remarkable in a rebuilt side after the departure of half the 1995 championship team.
"After 10 matches it was totally unreasonable to dream of (Europe)," he said.
Now unbeaten in 26 league matches, Nantes have suffered one defeat since October when they crashed to third division Vitrolles in the French Cup in January.
"After 20 (games), Europe became visible and now, five games from the finish, it's there, more than ever," Suaudeau said.

Suaudeau warned that down to seventh-placed defending champions Auxerre there are five teams in line for four places in Europe, three in the UEFA Cup, after Strasbourg's qualification as League Cup winners.
And although Nantes' goal difference is second only to Monaco's he does not believe his side's current form, particularly away, is any guarantee of success.
"On our last seven trips away we've taken 19 out of a possible 21 points, but still we're going to have to work."

Suaudeau said if the French first division had dropped in quality, it was due not so much to the exodus of many top players but rather because there was so much at stake, especially at the bottom with four teams facing relegation.
"We're playing longer (balls) this season, we're bypassing the midfield and the game's suffering, it's less attractive. At Nantes, that's not our style...but we've had to adapt."

He said his team's poor start to the season had been due both to a lack of proper preparation, interrupted by the Intertoto Cup, and a change in the way most of the teams in the first division were playing.
"I found I was off my game, simply because in the championship our adversaries' style was more direct. First I had to realise this and then stick more to the reality," he said.
The net result is a season divided into three distinct stages.
The first, the opening 10 games in which Nantes picked up only five points, was followed by a spell of high scoring.
Starting with their first victory of the season, 7-0 at home against Nice in October, they hit 31 goals in 11 games.
The third stage has seen them become almost impregnable in defence, conceding three goals in 12 matches while scoring 12.
"Three months ago we were scoring a lot of goals. Now, we don't concede any. Apart from the goal we conceded to Marseille (in the final minute to draw 1-1), we are hyper-effective," he Suaudeau said.
